Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology

Eadred.fact: He also invaded Mercia and Edmund was forced to surrender the Five Boroughs of north-east Mercia to him.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: Guthfrithson died in 941 and in 942, Edmund was able to recover the _____
Eadred.fact: He also invaded Mercia and Edmund was forced to surrender the Five Boroughs of north-east Mercia to him. Guthfrithson died in 941 and in 942, Edmund was able to recover the Five Boroughs.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: In 944, he recovered full control of _____ by expelling the Viking kings of York
Eadred.fact: In 944, he recovered full control of England by expelling the Viking kings of York.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: Æthelstan, the son of _____'s first wife, Ecgwynn, was born around 894, but she probably died around the time of Alfred's death, as by 901 Edward was married to Ælfflæd
Eadred.fact: Æthelstan, the son of Edward's first wife, Ecgwynn, was born around 894, but she probably died around the time of Alfred's death, as by 901 Edward was married to Ælfflæd. According to the twelfth-century chronicler William of Malmesbury, Edmund was about eighteen years old when he succeeded to the throne in 939, which dates his birth to 920–921, and their father Edward died in 924, so Eadred was born around 923.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: Eadgifu attested around one-third of _____'s charters, always as regis mater (king's mother), including all grants to religious institutions and individuals
Eadred.fact: Eadgifu and Eadred attested many of Edmund's charters, showing a high degree of family cooperation; initially Eadgifu attested first, but from sometime in late 943 or early 944 Eadred took precedence, perhaps reflecting his growing authority. Eadgifu attested around one-third of Edmund's charters, always as regis mater (king's mother), including all grants to religious institutions and individuals.

Eadred.fact: The Viking Anlaf Sihtricson (also called Olaf Sihtricson and Amlaib Cuaran) ruled Dublin and the southern Northumbrian kingdom of York at different periods.

When king of York in the early 940s, he had accepted baptism with Edmund as his godfather, indicating submission to his rule, and his coins followed English designs, but Edmund had expelled him in 944.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: The York magnates were key players, led by the powerful _____, Archbishop of York, who periodically made bids for independence by accepting Viking kings, but submitted to southern rule at other times
Eadred.fact: The York magnates were key players, led by the powerful Wulfstan, Archbishop of York, who periodically made bids for independence by accepting Viking kings, but submitted to southern rule at other times. In the view of the historian Marios Costambeys, Wulfstan's influence in Northumbria appears to have been greater than Erik's.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: In the view of the historian _____, Wulfstan's influence in Northumbria appears to have been greater than Erik's
Eadred.fact: In the view of the historian Marios Costambeys, Wulfstan's influence in Northumbria appears to have been greater than Erik's.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: According to the Anglo-_____, he immediately "reduced all Northumbria under his rule" and obtained promises of obedience from the Scots
Eadred.fact: The sequence of events is very unclear because different manuscripts of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle contradict each other, and they also conflict with the evidence of charters, which are the only contemporary sources. According to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, he immediately "reduced all Northumbria under his rule" and obtained promises of obedience from the Scots.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: He may have invaded _____ in response to a rebellion supported by the Scots
Eadred.fact: Charters of 946, 949–50 and 955 call Eadred ruler of the Northumbrians, and these provide evidence of periods when York submitted to southern rule. According to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, he immediately "reduced all Northumbria under his rule" and obtained promises of obedience from the Scots.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology

Eadred.fact: He was crowned by Archbishop Oda of Canterbury on 16 August 946 at Kingston upon Thames, attended by Hywel Dda, king of Deheubarth in south Wales, Wulfstan and Osulf.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: The following year at _____, near the border between Northumbria and Mercia, Wulfstan and the other York magnates pledged allegiance to him
Eadred.fact: The following year at Tanshelf, near the border between Northumbria and Mercia, Wulfstan and the other York magnates pledged allegiance to him.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: The York magnates soon reneged on their promises and accepted _____ as king
Eadred.fact: The York magnates soon reneged on their promises and accepted Erik as king.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology

Eadred.fact: Wulfstan was later released, probably in early 955, but he was apparently not allowed to resume his archbishopric and instead given the bishopric of Dorchester-on-Thames.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology

Eadred.fact: In his will, Eadred left 1600 pounds to be used for protection of his people from famine or to buy peace from a heathen army, showing that he did not regard England as safe from attack.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: Oda, _____ of Canterbury, and Ealdorman Æthelstan of East Anglia, had been advisers of King Æthelstan who had become dominant under Edmund
Eadred.fact: Eadred had been very close to Edmund and inherited many of his leading advisers, such as his mother Eadgifu, Oda, Archbishop of Canterbury, and Æthelstan, ealdorman of East Anglia, who was so powerful that he was called the "Half-King". Dunstan, Abbot of Glastonbury and future Archbishop of Canterbury, was a close friend and adviser, and Eadred appears to have authorised Dunstan to draft charters when he became too ill to attend meetings of the witan (King's Council) in his last years.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: His prestige was further increased when his wife Ælfwynn became foster-mother to _____'s younger son Edgar following his mother's early death
Eadred.fact: Eadred's principal councillors were mainly people he had inherited from his brother Edmund, and in a few cases went back to his half-brother Æthelstan. Oda, Archbishop of Canterbury, and Ealdorman Æthelstan of East Anglia, had been advisers of King Æthelstan who had become dominant under Edmund.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: Ælfgar, the father of _____'s second wife Æthelflæd, was ealdorman of Essex from 946 to 951
Eadred.fact: Eadgifu had been sidelined under the rule of her stepson Æthelstan, but she became powerful under the rule of her own sons Edmund and Eadred. Ælfgar, the father of Edmund's second wife Æthelflæd, was ealdorman of Essex from 946 to 951.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology
Eadred.question: Ælfgar consistently attested last among the ealdormen, and he may have been subordinate to Æthelstan _____-King
Eadred.fact: Ælfgar consistently attested last among the ealdormen, and he may have been subordinate to Æthelstan Half-King. Ealdormen issued legal judgments on behalf of the king at a local level.

Eadred.subject: Environment & Ecology

Eadred.fact: A man called Æthelstan of Sunbury was later found to have her in his possession and could not prove he had acquired her legally. He surrendered possession and paid compensation to the owner, but Ealdorman Byrhtferth ordered him to pay his wer (the value of his life) to the king, and when Æthelstan could not pay Byrhtferth required him to forfeit his Sunbury estate.

Eadwig.fact: He was the elder son of Edmund I and his first wife Ælfgifu, who died in 944. As Edmund's sons were too young to rule he was succeeded by his brother Eadred, who suffered from ill health and died unmarried in his early 30s.

Eadwig.subject: Environment & Ecology

Eadwig.subject: Environment & Ecology

Eadwig.subject: Environment & Ecology

Earl of Mar.fact: The issue remained unresolved until 1457, when James II obtained a court order declaring the lands as crown possessions. It was next granted to James' other son, Alexander, Duke of Albany, but the title was then declared forfeit because of Alexander's alliances with the English.

Earl of Mar.subject: Environment & Ecology
Earl of Mar.question: After the death of _____, his lands were passed to the sovereign in accordance with the charter, and thereafter were disposed of by the Crown
Earl of Mar.fact: The petition made a number of claims: The original Earldom of Mar was a territorial title rather than a title of peerage and was therefore "indivisible." (In other words, the territory could not be separated from the title.) Alexander Stewart obtained a new royal charter for the Earldom, rather than receiving it in right of his wife Isabel. After the death of Alexander Stewart, his lands were passed to the sovereign in accordance with the charter, and thereafter were disposed of by the Crown.

Only 1 to 2 percent of the energy from the sun is absorbed by photosynthetic processes and converted into food.  When energy is transferred to higher trophic levels, on average only about 10% is used at each level to build biomass, becoming stored energy. Catastrophic Climax Climax vegetation vulnerable to a catastrophic event such as a wildfire.  For example, in California, chaparral vegetation is the final vegetation.
